[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2022-43605:cve-2022-43605-summa:0e083bcc56b5 kind=issue issue=2022 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#CVE-2022-43605.txt]
Issue: CVE-2022-43605
Summary: In EIP Stack Group OpENer development commit 58ee13c, cipcommon.c:SetAttributeList uses the request-supplied attribute_count_request as the upper bound for the loop that appends attribute data to a CipMessageRouterResponse. A specially crafted EtherNet/IP SetAttributeList request with attribute_count_request greater than 0x80 can move outgoing_message->current_message_position outside the EnipMessage buffer, after which AddIntToMessage/AddSintToMessage in endianconv.c write past that buffer. The document describes stack corruption leading to a server/process crash and loss of communications, and states this may potentially allow code execution.
Reproduce: The advisory does not provide exact build commands or a full PoC. Documented reproduction is: 1) use EIP Stack Group OpENer development commit 58ee13c; 2) send the specially crafted EtherNet/IP request sequence that reaches SetAttributeList with attribute_count_request set to a value greater than 0x80; 3) during response construction, outgoing_message->current_message_position is incremented beyond the EnipMessage buffer and subsequent AddIntToMessage/AddSintToMessage calls write user-supplied data out of bounds. Expected result: stack corruption and a server/process crash with loss of communications. The document mentions code execution only as a potential outcome.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:564:564-summary:6b535e1b37b6 kind=issue issue=564 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#564.txt]
Issue: 564
Summary: OpENer commit 76b95cf has an out-of-bounds read in Connection Manager handling of malformed CIP ForwardOpen/LargeForwardOpen requests. `ForwardOpenRoutine()` in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionmanager.c` calls `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` before strict minimal-length validation, and that parser in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionobject.c` repeatedly uses `GetByteFromMessage()`, `GetUintFromMessage()`, and `GetUdintFromMessage()` in `source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c` without a remaining-readable-length parameter for per-read boundary checks. A valid ENIP frame carrying a malformed ForwardOpen or LargeForwardOpen with insufficient request data can therefore leave the input pointer at the end of the receive buffer and still make `GetByteFromMessage()` read past it. The supplied ASan run reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` / `READ of size 1` in `GetByteFromMessage`, reached via `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` and `ForwardOpenRoutine()`, overflowing the stack `incoming_message` buffer and aborting. The document states the issue is remotely triggerable over network traffic without authentication.
Reproduce: Prerequisites: the provided Python 3 PoC and an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer binary from commit 76b95cf. Use the PoC against its documented defaults (`--host 127.0.0.1 --port 44818 --timeout 1.5 --attempts 50 --interval-ms 50`) and select `--service forward-open` or `--service large-forward-open`. For each attempt, the client opens a TCP connection, sends ENIP `RegisterSession` (`0x0065`) to obtain a session handle, then sends a valid ENIP `SendRRData` (`0x006F`) frame with CPF `Null` and `UCMM` items. The UCMM item contains a malformed CIP payload: service `0x54` (ForwardOpen) or `0x5B` (LargeForwardOpen),

[SOURCE id=issue:567:567-summary:1255c28909d7 kind=issue issue=567 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#567.txt]
Issue: 567
Summary: On the latest master branch of OpENer, the report describes a remotely reachable server-side crash triggered by a crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request. The report attributes the underlying corruption to request handling before the visible crash: CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure() accepts a malformed CPF with an invalid item_count/inconsistent length, the unconnected Message Router payload reaches GetAttributeList(), GetAttributeList() parses an attacker-controlled excessively large attribute_count_request and builds an oversized inner Message Router response, and EncodeMessageRouterResponseData() copies that inner response into the outer ENIPMessage without validating remaining destination capacity. According to the report, this overruns message_buffer[512] and overwrites the adjacent current_message_position field; the observed result is that AddIntToMessage() later dereferences the corrupted pointer and crashes. The documented crash is an AddressSanitizer SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136.
Reproduce: 1) Use the latest master branch of OpENer and run a server instance; the report demonstrates the issue on an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer build. 2) Send the provided crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request to the server. The PoC is the hex byte sequence beginning with <6f><00><30><01><30><30><30><30> and continuing exactly as provided in the document. 3) Observe the server abort under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136:49, with the stack including EncodeSockaddrInfoItemTypeId(), AssembleLinearMessage(), NotifyCommonPacketFormat(), HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand(), and HandleReceivedExplictTcpData().
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:570:570-summary:0b4cbe808107 kind=issue issue=570 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#570.txt]
Issue: 570
Summary: A malformed `ForwardOpen` request can trigger a network-reachable out-of-bounds read in OpENer during connection-path parsing. In `ParseConnectionPath()`, the trailing Simple Data Segment length byte is trusted without checking that it still fits the remaining path budget, so `remaining_path` can underflow and `message` can be advanced past the request buffer. The next `GetPathSegmentType(message)` access then reads out of bounds and crashes the server. The reachable path shown is `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()` -> `HandleReceivedExplictTcpData()` -> `HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand()` -> `NotifyCommonPacketFormat()` -> `NotifyMessageRouter()` -> `NotifyClass()` -> `ForwardOpen()` -> `ForwardOpenRoutine()` -> `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` -> `ParseConnectionPath()` -> `GetPathSegmentType()`. `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` calls `ParseConnectionPath()` before any `open_connection_function` is called.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against an OpENer server listening on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script registers a session, wraps a CIP `ForwardOpen` request to Connection Manager class `0x06`, instance `1`, inside `SendRRData`, and sends it over TCP 44818. It supports `baseline` and `crash`; `baseline` uses the valid path `20 04 24 97 2C 96 2C 64`, while `crash` appends `80 FF` so the trailing Simple Data Segment claims `0xff` words with only one word left. Command: `python3 poc.py crash`. On the vulnerable server, `ParseConnectionPath()` underflows `remaining_path`, advances past the request buffer, and `GetPathSegmentType()` dereferences out of bounds and crashes the server.
[/SOURCE]
